<note>A hand-shaped pointer marks the following text.</note> I was coagulated in the time of ten months in the blood from the seed of man and the pleasure of sleep accompanying it.

Verse 2. In the womb of the mother I was formed in the flesh in the time of ten months, coagulated in blood, from the seed of man and the pleasure accompanying sleep.

*Ten months, etc.* As a commoner, in the maternal womb, the site of which is between the bladder and the intestines. Hence the exclamation of Realdo Colombo, the Roman anatomist: *O man, why do you boast with empty pride, born between urine and excrement!* Consider, I beg you, my brother, what you are, and you will cease to be proud: is there not stench at the beginning, a bubble in all of life, and food for worms in death? Elsewhere also in the sacred writings, man is called *clay* (Gen. 2:7, Job 10:9), *dust* (Gen. 3:19), *ashes* (Gen. 18:27). *Why then do you boast, earth and ashes?* (Ecclesiastes 10:9).
*Since we are mud and slime, since we are the most shameful filth:*
*Why do we boast, when we do not know when we die.*

12 Furthermore, when born, I inhaled the common air, and fell upon the earth, which is subject to the same inconveniences and evils, and I uttered the same first voice as everyone else, crying.

Verse 3. And I, when born, received the common air, and fell into the earth, which is fated in a similar way, and I emitted the first voice, similar to everyone, crying.

*First voice.* What is that? Perhaps A for males; E for females; as the Nobleman von Eib, Doctor of Laws, noted when dealing with marriage; and midwives who have observed this affirm. *Crying.* And he is thus (as Augustine says) a prophet of his own future calamity. Whence Job 13:1: *Man born of woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries.* Sirach (chap. 40) adds the reason. For it is, as Seneca witnesses, the end of one evil is the preparation for another. This, Job experienced egregiously, saying in chapter 7, verses 3 and 4: *I have had empty months, and I have numbered to myself laborious nights. If I sleep, I say: when shall I arise? and again I will look for the evening, and I will be filled with sorrows even until evening. <margin>Job 1:21. 1 Tim. 6:7.</margin>
15 | There is therefore one entry for all to life, and a similar exit. | <margin>Ver. 6.</margin> But there is one entry for all into life, and the same exit. | 15

*A similar exit*] The Catholic <note>meaning universal</note> law set for all is to die once. Hebrews 9:27. *The way of death must be trodden by all*, says Horace (Odes, Book 1). Cornelius Gallus rightly says: *The way of death is the same for all, though not one; the manner of life and of ruin is for everyone.*

Consider therefore, my brother, how this life is more fleeting than smoke, more empty than a shadow. For the days of our life flee like a shadow (1 Chronicles 29:15; Job 8:9, 14:2; Psalm 109:23, 144:4; Ecclesiastes 7:1; Wisdom 2:5, 5:9). *They vanish like smoke* (Psalm 102:4). *They pass more swiftly than the thread is cut by the weaver* (Job 7:6). *They are swifter than a runner* (Job 9:25). *They meditate like a spider* (Psalm 90:9). *They are as a watch in the night* (Psalm 90:4, 6). *Our life is wind* (Job 7:7). *It is a vapor that appears for a little while and is then destroyed* (James 4:14). *It passes like a cloud* (Psalm 7:9). *All flesh is grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field, blooming in the morning and falling in the evening* (Isaiah 40:6-7; Job 14:2; Psalm 90:4, 6; Ecclesiastes 14:18). Considering this fragility of human life on one hand, and the infinite amplitude of the Divine Majesty on the other, the Royal Prophet is seized with wonder and, as if astonished, breaks out into this voice: *What is man, that you are mindful of him?* (Psalm 8:5). This same thought also drew tears from Xerxes, that valiant and most powerful King, when from a high and lofty place he beheld an infinite multitude of men and an innumerable army, because none of those whom he then saw would be alive after one hundred years. Therefore, compensate for this brevity of life with goodness and integrity, you who profess yourself a Christian; do not think of how long you live, but how well. And since nothing is more certain than death, yet nothing more uncertain than the hour of death, learn to die well by living holily in the fear of GOD.

16 | And He (my Father) taught Me, and said: Let your heart receive my words, keep my precepts, and you shall live. | <margin>Prov. 4:4.</margin> He himself taught me, and said to me: Let your heart hold my sayings: keep my precepts, and you shall live. | 16

*And you shall live*] You shall be long-lived upon the earth, and you shall enjoy life hereafter in eternity, in the final Jubilee. Life flows from the word of life. The word of GOD is Spirit and life: therefore, the guardian of the life-giving word shall have life as a reward.

<margin>He commands that Wisdom, its fruit, and its way be sought.</margin>
17 | <note>A small hand-shaped pointer marks the following text.</note> Possess WISDOM, possess PRUDENCE: do not forget; <note>A small hand-shaped pointer marks the following text.</note> nor decline from the words of my mouth. | <margin>Ver. 5.</margin> Acquire WISDOM, acquire UNDERSTANDING: do not forget, nor decline from the sayings of my mouth. | 17

*Possess WISDOM.*] For GOD loves no one except him who dwells with WISDOM, or has fellowship with her, says the Wise Man, verse 300. *Nor decline.*] He who departs from the sayings of GOD can never approach GOD Himself, the fountain of WISDOM.

These are the constellations of success <note>Sanskrit: *siddhinakshatrani*</note>, which are recognized by those skilled in the science of non-weapons <note>likely referring to astrology or peaceful sciences</note>. For these, one should undertake
actions related to journeys, as well as nourishing <note>Sanskrit: *paustika*</note> and pacifying <note>Sanskrit: *shantika*</note> rituals. In the constellation of Pushya, the following are successful: traveling by chariot, the treatment of eyes, and <insert>11</insert> one should perform the commencement of a journey. However, if one is already engaged in an activity, it may lead to loss of wealth or fear. Actions involving poison,
waking, using a staff, medicine, making holes, entering a cavity, or dealing with wicked people and various fears <margin>11</margin> 2. One should perform storytelling, debates, and various types of selection. Regarding the enemy's metal, first perform the act of burying. <insert>11</insert>
All funeral rites, granaries, sowing of seeds, rules for building a house <insert>43</insert>, and the initiation
of all aquatic activities, matters of passion and increase, and the use of poisonous rays. For new kings, the collection of taxes, or seeking refuge in a city, these are the actions. <insert>15</insert> Dealing with friends, medicine, plowing, taking up a crown, and approaching merchants.

### Bottom Fragment

<margin>
Journeys to other lands are generally not praised. One should understand the calculation of the two... writing is superior. Knowledge, pacifying and nourishing rituals, and the performance of tasks—all these are successful actions. Thus ends the Section on Varuna <note>Sanskrit: *Varuna Kanda*</note>. One should know the rules of action and weapons, but not the authority of knowledge.
</margin>

...in selection... of the two... trade and merchants, and the excellence of others. One should perform these for the sake of a son...
<margin>...wind and water...</margin>
...fame, marriage, meritorious acts, royal duties, initiation, and the protection of living beings. In the constellation of Uttaraphalguni <insert>7</insert>, one achieves success in actions involving horses, elephants, and the intoxicating rut of animals.
The building of stables for elephants, knowledge, pacifying and nourishing rituals, the gift of cows, and the performance of sacrifices.
The taming of horses, the best of faces, and the success of intoxication...
One should perform <insert>3</insert> trade, the work of dancers, and the inspection of the king's army.
Knowledge, the destruction of enemies, and royal duties are accomplished. In the constellation of Chitra, one should perform various
canopies, the playing of musical instruments, and the planting of trees. The taking of these two, and the taming of donkeys, camels, and horses.

### — 5. Characteristics of Wells

<margin>The proximity of the roots will be described in various ways; the use of roots in the sowing of seeds and the essence of medicinal herbs.</margin>
Success is achieved at the root for those who strive in their work <gloss>34</gloss>. The bird of the beloved lamented, O Master, O Master, upon the branch of the willow tree.
Allah, Allah, Allah, our Lord, Allah, Allah, Allah is sufficient for us, and the Prophet, the Chosen One, is our beloved, O our Master.
The wound of the heart from passion does not heal.
How can it heal when inside the heart is a glowing coal, O our Master?
O you full moon, I have no patience to be away from you.
How can I be patient when I have fallen in love with a full moon, O our Master?
Allah, Allah, Master of Masters, Allah, Allah, O Knower of my state.
I entrusted you, so protect me with safety, O reaching the peace of the possessor of the mark.
Muhammad, sent from Tihama <note>The coastal region of the Arabian Peninsula</note>, the guardian of passion, the Reservoir <note>The Prophet's pool in Paradise</note>, and the honors.
There is no god but Allah, Allah, Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, my Master, O Muhammad.
I have no beloved [but] the Prophet of Allah, then the one with the languid gaze, the perfected one...
If he is absent from my eyes, then Allah, he is fashioned into the heart, my Master, O Muhammad.
O Sultan, O Possessor, and upon your servant, [mercy], [mercy].

<column-break/>

In a heart other than yours from you, O Sultan, O Possessor.
The ransom of my secret, Sultan, the salvation of the mark.
Upon you, upon you, O her purity.
O Sultan, daughter of the people of prayer.
O possessor of the cannon <note>possibly a metaphorical reference to spiritual power or a signal for breaking fast</note>, my heart...
Allah, Allah, then Allah, Allah, Allah, and the Generous is Allah.
You have robbed the intellect from the wise ones at night, O hand, have mercy on the slain [lovers].
I am wandering, distracted by their driver, O [you who are] alone, let me be, slowly.
Ahmad, Muhammad, grandfather, peace be upon him, glory, the glory of the Master.
A Master who has been made a leader of the people.
You are Taha, for me you are, for me you are the best protector.
I am the servant of Allah, eternally my Master, a Master who has been made a leader of the people.
And upon your good deeds, always cover me.

<summary>Devotional verses expressing the pain of spiritual longing and love for the Prophet Muhammad, referred to as the Sultan and the full moon.</summary>

<meta>This folio, numbered 74, continues a dialogue regarding the spiritual and social order of a community. While the previous page (Page 1) was an introductory invocation to Shiva, this page appears much further into the text, focusing on the necessity of ritual, the presence of wise Brahmins in a village, and the consequences of neglecting sacred duties. The speaker—likely a deity or high sage—is addressing the requirements for a "Great Sacrifice" and the preservation of purity.</meta>

<margin>
Folio 74
</margin>

"Without her, how can there even be a village or a <term>Great Sacrifice</term> <note>original: "Mahayajna"; refers to the five daily sacrifices or a major public ritual in the Vedic tradition.</note> here?" As <term>Brahma</term> <note>The creator god in the Hindu triad.</note> said: "In a place where there is no wise <term>Brahmana</term> <note>A member of the priestly class, responsible for maintaining sacred knowledge.</note> skilled in hundreds of words, a wise man should enter that village again [with caution]." **1** "I should not establish a dwelling here."

If there is a good physician, and yet there is no performer of the great ritual or one who removes impurities, [it is incomplete]. I shall proclaim my view here; listen to it always. Therefore, O <term>Brahmana</term>, listen to this delightful rite that brings <term>Shanti</term> <note>original: "Shantipradam"; a ritual intended to bring peace, avert evil, or provide atonement.</note>. If it is not performed there, the <term>Maharshis</term> <note>The "Great Sages" or ancient seers of divine truth.</note> say a fault is incurred.

In the three journeys and in the <term>Three Worlds</term> <note>original: "Trailokye"; the cosmos divided into earth, atmosphere, and heaven.</note>, she is saluted without the Goddess. As it is said: "One who is at the mouth of the vessel of the ritual as before, he [attains] the fruit of <term>Dharma</term> <note>The eternal law, duty, and righteousness that upholds the cosmos.</note> on this earth, as does <term>Maheshvara</term> <note>The "Great Lord," a title for Shiva.</note>." To the ignorant, he is the giver of Dharma.

Just as it is with those two, so it is: "Humans and my son are always pure in the six [duties]." All this is ordained through my own nature/state. The man who performs this has no fault/sin; he is liberated from all sins.

One should point out the death [associated with] <term>Sura</term> <note>An intoxicating spirit or wine, often forbidden or strictly regulated in Brahminical law.</note>. With great effort, protect the youth who has come to your house. Outer purity is then his guardian and protector. Whoever would feed a <term>Brahmana</term> in whose hand [the sacred] is always held, he attains perpetual Brahminhood.

One should not drink <term>Madya</term> <note>Alcohol or intoxicating liquor.</note>... and so others. "As you wish, so listen to me, O best of speakers." Having said this, [the speaker] paused. **6** The <term>Rishis</term> <note>The Sages.</note> said: "How does the wise man exist in the realm of humans? How is this?"

<summary>This page discusses the essential components of a righteous village, emphasizing the presence of wise Brahmins and the performance of "Shanti" (peace-giving) rituals. It concludes with the Sages asking how a truly wise person can live within the mundane world of ordinary humans.</summary>
<keywords>Mahayajna, Brahmana, Shanti, Dharma, Maheshvara, ritual purity, social order, Maharshis, intoxicating spirits</keywords>

<meta>Following the discourse on the necessity of ritual and the presence of wise priests on page 74, this page provides a specific liturgical tool: the Navakshari (Nine-Syllable) Mantra and its accompanying ritual manual. It shifts from the "why" of ritual to the "how," offering a direct method for the practitioner to invoke the Goddess.</meta>

ॐ Salutations to <term>Vinayaka</term> <note>original: "Vinayakaya"; another name for Ganesha, the elephant-headed god who removes obstacles and is traditionally invoked first.</note> || Salutations to the Sun || Salutations to <term>Shiva</term> <note>The destroyer and transformer within the Hindu trinity.</note> || Salutations to <term>Narayana</term> <note>A name for Vishnu, the sustainer of the universe.</note> || Salutations to <term>Saraswati</term> <note>The goddess of knowledge, music, and the arts.</note> || Salutations to <term>Kamadeva</term> <note>The god of love and desire.</note> || Salutations to the venerable Teacher || Salutations to all the gods || Salutations to the family deities || Salutations to the personal chosen deities ||

Of this sacred <term>Navakshari Vidya Mantra</term> <note>original: "Navakshari-vidya-mantra"; the "Nine-Syllable Knowledge Mantra," also known as the Navarna Mantra, dedicated to the supreme Goddess.</note>, the Seer is <term>Brahma</term> <note>The creator god who first "saw" or received the mantra.</note>, the poetic meter is <term>Gayatri</term>, and the deities are the Great Kali, the Great Lakshmi, and the Great Saraswati || The "seed" syllable is *Aim* || The power is *Hrim* || The "pin" is *Klim* <note>original: "Kilaka"; a syllable that acts as a lock or focal point for the mantra's energy.</note> ||

The ritual application <note>original: "viniyoga"</note> of this chanting is for the fulfillment of all my heart's desires || Now follows the **Hand-Placement** <note>original: "Karanyasa"; a ritual where the practitioner touches parts of the hand while reciting syllables to "place" the deity's power into their body.</note> || ॐ *Aim*, salutations to the two thumbs || ॐ *Hrim*, salutations to the two index fingers || ॐ *Klim*, salutations to the two middle fingers || ॐ *Chamundayai*, salutations to the two ring fingers ||

In this same way, the placement of mantras on the heart and other limbs is performed || Now for the **Meditation** <note>original: "Dhyanam"; a descriptive verse used to visualize the deity before chanting.</note> || I bow to the goddess <term>Chamunda</term> <note>A fierce, protective form of the Divine Mother.</note>, the crusher of the demon Munda; she resembles a heap of blue eye-ointment, carries a trident, a discus, and a mace, and her face bears a gentle smile || Thus ends the meditation ||

**ॐ Aim Hrim Klim Chamundayai Vicche**

**The Meaning of the Mantra:**
The syllable *Aim* is the very form of creation; the syllable *Hrim* is the sustainer of existence || The syllable *Klim* is the form of desire, and Chamunda is the crusher of the demon Munda ||
The syllable *Yai* is the eternal giver of boons, and *Vicche* is the granter of fearlessness || Thus, this Nine-Syllable Knowledge bestows all perfections ||

Thus ends the **Hymn of the Nine-Syllable Mantra** || May there be auspiciousness || <unclear>॥</unclear>

<keywords>Navarna Mantra, Chamunda, Karanyasa (hand-placement), Dhyana (meditation), Devi, Shakti, Sanskrit ritual, Stotra</keywords>

<margin>
निशुं
भवधः

विचिन्त्यैवं विनिष्क्रांतो भ्रात्रा सह निशुंभेन॥ यतश्च सुमहारत्नानि सर्वाण्येव हतानि मे॥ स वै मया तु निहतः सङ्ख्ये भ्राता निशुंभकः॥ १८॥ तं मया हतमाज्ञाय संक्रुद्धः शुंभ दानवः॥
सागतः परसैन्येन निहंतुं चंडिकां रणे॥ तमायांतं विलोक्याह चंडिका परमेश्वरी॥ १८॥ मयि तिष्ठति यस्त्वं वै संक्रुद्धः किं करिष्यसि॥ १९॥ तामुवाच ततः शुंभो मदोद्धत मुखांबुजः॥
कः शक्तो मां रणे जेतुं चराचर गुरुं शिवे॥ २०॥ तमुवाच ततः सापि चंडिका मंदहासिनी॥ २१॥ अहं ब्रह्मविदि मन्ये मय्येव लयमेष्यति॥ २२॥ तच्छ्रुत्वा स महादैत्यः प्राह वाक्यं नराधिप॥
अहो विचित्र मेतद्धि चित्रमुत्पादयत्यहो॥ २३॥ ममाग्रतः स्थिता ह्येषां मयि सा लीन मेष्यति॥ २४॥ सा तथेत्युक्त्वा तं प्राह दानवेंद्रं महासुरं॥ २५॥ श्रुणु त्वं च महादैत्य
प्रवृत्ते समरे तस्मिन् भ्रातुस्तव निपातिते॥ २६॥ एतत्तव प्रकथितं शृणु मे वचनं शुभं॥ २७॥ तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा शुंभः क्रोध समन्वितः॥ प्रहारं च महाघोरं चकार स रणांगणे॥
बाणैस्तीक्ष्णैः सुपुखैश्च बाणवृष्टिमकारयत्॥ २८॥ तां तथा बाणवर्षेण छाद्यमानां विलोक्य सः॥ स चापि प्राह संक्रुद्धः प्रहारं च तदाऽकरोत्॥ तस्य शस्त्राणि शस्त्रास्त्रैः प्रतिहत्य स चंडिका॥
बिभेद तस्य गात्राणि स वै भीतः प्रधावितः॥ २९॥ वदंत्यति महाघोरं संक्रुद्धः स महासुरः॥ ३०॥ स धावन् सहसा देवी निजघान रणांगणे॥ ३१॥ दैत्याधिपतिमुद्दिश्य संक्रुद्धोऽसि विमूर्छिता॥

<meta>Following the ritual instructions for the Navakshari Mantra on page 74, this page transitions into the narrative of the *Devi Mahatmya* (The Glory of the Goddess). It illustrates the practical power of the deity invoked in the previous ritual, focusing on the psychological and physical confrontation between the Goddess Chandika and the demon-king Shumbha.</meta>

75

<margin>
The Slaying
of Nishumbha
</margin>

Thinking thus, he went forth with his brother **Nishumbha**. "Since all my great jewels have been seized, my brother **Nishumbhaka** was indeed killed by me in battle." || 18 || <note>This verse seems to reflect Shumbha's internal monologue or a summary of his loss before the fight.</note> Knowing him to be slain, the demon **Shumbha** was filled with rage. He arrived with a great army to slay **Chandika** <note>The "Fierce One," a powerful, warrior form of the Mother Goddess.</note> in battle. Seeing him approaching, **Chandika**, the Supreme Goddess, said: || 18 || "While I stand here, what will you, in your anger, truly achieve?" || 19 || Then **Shumbha**, his lotus-face arrogant with pride, spoke to her: "Who is able to defeat me in battle—the master of all things moving and unmoving, O **Shiva**?" <note>original: "Shive"; the feminine form of Shiva, addressing the Goddess as the Auspicious One.</note> || 20 || Then she, **Chandika**, with a gentle smile, spoke to him: || 21 || "I consider you a knower of the Absolute; <note>original: "brahmavidi"; one who understands the nature of Brahman or ultimate reality.</note> you shall find your end by merging into me alone." || 22 || Hearing that, the great demon spoke these words, O King: "Ah, how strange this is! It produces such wonder!" || 23 || "Standing here before me, she claims that I will merge into her!" || 24 || Saying "So be it," she then spoke to the great demon, the Lord of the Asuras: || 25 || "Listen, O Great Demon, now that the battle has begun and your brother has fallen— || 26 || Hear these auspicious words of mine." || 27 || Hearing her words, **Shumbha**, consumed by wrath, delivered a most terrible blow upon the battlefield. With sharp, well-feathered arrows, he unleashed a rain of shafts. || 28 || Seeing her thus covered by the rain of arrows, he, enraged, struck again. But **Chandika**, parrying his weapons with her own divine arms, pierced his body, and he fled in fear. || 29 || That great demon, extremely enraged, let out a most terrifying cry. || 30 || As he was running, the Goddess suddenly struck him down on the battlefield. || 31 || Aiming at the Lord of the Demons, you are enraged and fainted... <note>original: "vimurchita"; suggesting the demon was stunned or knocked unconscious by the divine strike.</note>

<vocab>Nishumbha, Chandika, Shumbha, Demon, Battlefield, The Absolute, Lord of the Demons, Slaying</vocab>

<summary>This page recounts the climactic battle between the Goddess Chandika and the demon king Shumbha, where the Goddess asserts that the demon's ultimate fate is to be absorbed back into her divine essence.</summary>

They obtain the fruit of the non-returner; they obtain it; they will obtain it. They obtain the state of an Arhat <gloss>one who has overcome the inner enemies</gloss>; they obtain it; they will obtain it. Even those of the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddha <gloss>Solitary Realizer</gloss>, by training in this very perfection of wisdom, have become perfectly awakened in their own enlightenment; they are becoming perfectly awakened; they will become perfectly awakened. Also the Bodhisattva Mahasattvas, by training in this very perfection of wisdom, have entered the faultless state of a Bodhisattva; they enter it; they will enter it. They have become perfectly and unexcelled awakened in complete enlightenment; they are becoming perfectly awakened; they will become perfectly awakened. Koushika, therefore, if a son of noble family or daughter of noble family desires to honor the Tathagatas, the Arhats, the perfectly completed Buddhas in person with flowers, garlands, incense, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, victory banners, flags, and various musical instruments; and desires to show respect...

I myself also honor, respect, serve, and make offerings to this perfection of wisdom. Since I thus honor, respect, serve, make offerings and engage with it, Koushika, what need is there to mention that a son of noble family or daughter of noble family who desires to become perfectly awakened in unexcelled and complete enlightenment should honor, respect, serve, and make offerings to this perfection of wisdom with flowers, garlands, incense, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, victory banners, flags, and various musical instruments? ...are the perfectly completed Buddhas. Those who arise from the <term>Tathagatas</term>, the <term>Arhats</term>, the perfectly completed Buddhas, are the Hearers and the <term>Pratyekabuddhas</term> <gloss>Solitary Realizers</gloss>. <term>Kaushika</term>, therefore, the sons and daughters of noble family of the Bodhisattva vehicle, or the sons and daughters of noble family of the Hearer vehicle or the <term>Pratyekabuddha</term> vehicle, should honor, respect, revere, and worship this very perfection of wisdom with flowers, garlands, incense, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, victory banners, flags, and various musical instruments. Thus, those sons or daughters of noble family who train in this will awaken, are awakening, and will awaken to unexcelled, perfectly complete enlightenment. Those of the Hearer vehicle will also attain, are attaining, and will attain the state of an <term>Arhat</term>. Those of the <term>Pratyekabuddha</term> vehicle will also attain, are attaining, and will attain the enlightenment of a <term>Pratyekabuddha</term>. This concludes the twenty-second chapter from the "Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Verses." Then the Blessed One...

<leaf-break/>

...has occurred, is attained, and will be attained. By those who have correctly entered into unexcelled, perfectly complete enlightenment, many such extensive teachings were shown, such as entering, having entered, and being about to enter into the faultless state of a Bodhisattva, and having awakened, being awakening, and being about to awaken to unexcelled, perfectly complete enlightenment. <term>Kaushika</term>, what are those extensively taught untainted phenomena? They are as follows: the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of concentration, and the perfection of wisdom. Emptiness of the internal, emptiness of the external, emptiness of the internal and external, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, emptiness beyond extremes, emptiness without beginning or end, emptiness of non-rejection, emptiness of nature, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of specific characteristics, and emptiness of non-observation...

How can this be a characteristic? The "state of being produced by fire" is not what is inferred; rather, fire itself is what is inferred by those who want to remove cold or to cook. The fulfillment of that need does not come from the nature of smoke as "fire-produced," but from the fire itself. Therefore, it is not logical to say that "having fire" is the characteristic of "having smoke." 

What is meant by "having smoke"? In the Buddhist view, it is smoke and the mountain. In the view of Kaṇāda <note>Vaisheshika</note>, there are additional things like conjunction <term>saṃyoga</term>, inherence <term>samavāya</term>, and the unseen force <term>adṛṣṭa</term>. Similarly, one must consider "having fire." 

In that case, if we analyze these two positions in parts—by twos, by threes, or all together—how could the status of "essential nature" <term>svabhāvatva</term> be consistent? For one thing cannot be the nature of another. Even if one imagines it so because of a final unity through inherence, nothing would be the nature of anything. 

A "characteristic" <term>lakṣaṇa</term> is said to be the nature itself that makes its own exclusion from different classes known. It is that "by which something is marked." The term "characteristic" is not used for things that are merely useful for production. If it were, then any cause would be a characteristic. 

Having refuted the opponent's idea of "mere causality," he asks: what more is gained by accepting their idea of "mere characteristic"? It is just a different way of saying the same thing, since there is no difference in the object itself. 

Moreover, even a mere nature is not a characteristic; rather, the "indicator" <term>jñāpaka</term> is. The indicator should properly be placed within the means of knowledge <term>pramāṇa</term>, not the object of knowledge <term>prameya</term>. 

Therefore, what is said following the "difficult to understand" view of Dharmottara <note>a famous Buddhist commentator</note>—namely:

"The characteristic of the thing to be known..." 

...is simply incorrect. To explain: a characteristic is used to remove disagreement regarding a specific type of direct perception that is distinct from other types of knowledge like inference. It is said: "A characteristic is stated by referring to the thing to be characterized." That which is well-known in the world as its characteristic is not known to the deluded; because it is a point of disagreement, it is stated as something to be taught by the treatise <term>śāstra</term>. As was said before:

"The means of knowledge are well-known..."

"...the treatise serves to turn away delusion."

In the same way, at the time of inference, "having fire" is not so well-known just by looking at "having smoke" that a characteristic—as something pervaded—would serve only to turn away delusion. We do not see what is harmed by using the word "cause" <term>nimitta</term> or what is gained by using the word "characteristic" <term>lakṣaṇa</term>, since the questions and answers remain the same. 

To explain: Why is this alone its cause? Because this alone is its characteristic. If someone then asks: Why is this alone its characteristic? If the answer is: "Because any other group of things besides what is intended as this characteristic is not its characteristic, due to the flaws of impossibility, non-pervasion, or over-pervasion," then why not just say: "This much alone is its cause because there is no other cause, due to the same flaws of impossibility and so on"? Would saying it that way make the speaker crooked or distorted? 

If you say these flaws are well-known in refuting a "characteristic," are they not also well-known in refuting a "cause"? It is common knowledge in the world that a cause is invalid if flaws like impossibility are present. Whenever something is refuted, it is by showing a flaw, and these flaws—impossibility and so on—are universal. 

For example, "earth" is not the inherent cause <term>samavāyin</term> of sound. Even if earth exists, sound may not <note>impossibility</note>, and sound may exist where earth does not <note>over-pervasion</note>. Thus, impossibility, non-pervasion, and so on are brought up as flaws to prove a point. 

Furthermore, the characteristic of an existing thing is not a single nature alone. Causes, effects, and companions that are invariable can all be characteristics. If you say "only the nature of being its cause is the characteristic," that is not right, because that itself needs to be characterized. 

Moreover, one must prove either that "not having fire" is not the characteristic of "having smoke" (because it would lead to flaws like impossibility), or one must prove the use of that term itself. In that case, someone might say that is the "thing to be proven" <term>sādhya</term>, as in other types of non-perception <term>anupalabdhi</term>. In that context, the absence of a characteristic is not directly perceived, because if it were, it would be illogical to bring up arguments like "impossibility." Therefore, it is based on inference...

<summary>Abhinavagupta argues that "cause" and "characteristic" are functionally similar in logic. He explains that a valid logical mark must avoid the three classic flaws: impossibility, being too narrow (non-pervasion), or being too broad (over-pervasion).</summary>

<meta>continues from previous page: Moreover, the characteristic of an existing thing is not a single nature alone. Causes, effects, and companions that are invariable can all be characteristics. If you say "only the nature of being its cause is the characteristic," that is not right, because that itself needs to be characterized. Moreover</meta>

it must be stated that there is a certainty of being <term>bhāva-niścaya</term> <gloss>the determination of existence</gloss>. This brings us back to what the ancient teachers believed: that one removes the mass of unwanted possibilities through <term>bādhaka-pramāṇa</term> <gloss>sublating evidence or contradictory proof</gloss>. 

One might ask: does this lead to an infinite regress <term>anavasthā</term> in inference? Does a mere change in name cause the flaws of the object, such as impossibility <term>asambhava</term>, to vanish? Even if we call it "reasoning" <term>yukti</term>, does the infinite regress persist? 

To explain: impossibility in the case of fire and smoke is simply the absence of possibility. "Possibility" here refers to the smoke itself, meaning the existence of smoke or its inherent relation to its cause. If the absence of that smoke is internal to the nature of consciousness, taking the form of non-perception <term>anupalambha</term>, then it rests on the direct perception of one's own consciousness <term>svasaṃvedana-pratyakṣa</term>. If it is external, then it is an object with a different nature, which must be grasped by another means of knowledge, such as direct perception. 

In that context, the objection regarding the universal nature of the cause and so on can also be raised here. If we say that the possibility of smoke is not seen in a wall or in fire, but it might be possible in some other place, like the realm of ghosts <term>piśāca</term>, how can we be sure? If someone says, "If it were impossible there as well, then smoke would not be possible even here," then we must consider this: how do we know that some invisible ghost-like entity is not the producer of smoke here? 

If it is argued that if smoke came from such an entity, it would not depend on fire and would exist even in the absence of fire, but we see that is not the case, then alas! This means that the proof is based on non-perception <term>anupalambha</term>, which grasps the absence <term>vyatireka</term>. Thus, the causal relation <term>kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva</term> is established through the five-fold method of perception and non-perception <note>a logical method of determining causality by observing when two things appear and disappear together</note>. This rests upon the reality of one's own reflexive consciousness, which is the proper interior view of our system. 

In this matter, the certainty of universality is determined through worldly practice, through learning, through scripture, or through one's own intuition <term>pratibhā</term> arising from practice in previous lives. This power, which is actually the fixed power of the Lord <term>bhagavan-niyata-śakti</term>, should be described as the effective force, rather than just talking about "impossibility" and similar flaws. Even when these flaws are pointed out, they take the form of an argument by consequence <term>prasaṅga-sādhana</term>, and since they prove what is intended in their own way, they do not go beyond the scope of inference. A proof or a refutation is never based on something that is not a means of knowledge. A proof or refutation that correctly makes known the validity or correctness of a point is indeed a means of knowledge <term>pramāṇa</term>, because its very nature is to provide knowledge.

# Chapter Four

## The Goddess said:

I ask one thing, O highly fortunate one, Lord of Yogis, who is kind to devotees. Tell me now the secret of the Kali age, O Shankara <gloss>the Giver of Bliss, a name of Shiva</gloss>. (1)

## The Illustrious Ishana <gloss>the Ruler, a name of Shiva</gloss> said:

By Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras, and intermediate castes, worship and recitation should be performed in the Kali age with the animal disposition <note>original: "Pashu-bhava"</note>. (2)
The divine disposition <note>original: "Divya-bhava"</note> and the heroic disposition <note>original: "Vira-bhava"</note> do not exist in the Kali age. Perform three daily baths and worship with vegetarian sacrificial offerings. (3)
A Shudra should not drink intoxicants; by drinking, he becomes a murderer of a Brahmin. Having performed the morning bath, he should worship according to the sequence of the chapters. (4)
Or listen, O fair-limbed one, I will speak briefly. Whether impure or pure, whether walking, standing, or sleeping, (5)
 the wise man who remembers the mantra should always practice it mentally. In the Kali age, there is no preliminary rite <note>original: "Purashcharana"</note> because people are afflicted by hunger and sleep. (6)
Listen, I shall tell you the secret of Shiva worship. By performing it, one becomes a lord of success and may wander upon the circle of the earth. (7)
One should worship the Shiva-linga <gloss>the phallic emblem of Shiva</gloss> according to the rule of Shiva's mantra. The mantra "Om Namah Shivaya" is not approved for Shudras. (8)
The mantra "Namah Shivaya" <gloss>Salutation to Shiva</gloss> is the one recommended for the Shudra classes. The ritual placement <note>original: "Nyasa"</note> should be the placement of letters <note>original: "Matrika-nyasa"</note> joined with sixteen crores. (9)
One of steady mind should perform the placement joined with the fourteen vowels. Listen to the practical application, O fair-limbed one, I speak it, O woman of excellent face. (10)
"Om Yum Om Namo" on the forehead, "Om Shrim Am Om Am Om" on the mouth. In such a manner, O fair-limbed one, one should perform the ritual placement with a concentrated mind. (11)

וקא משחנא עדניא וזמניא וכלהו חיזו כדסותיה וחפיק לעמיק קליפא מחולא ורסוקא דככביא ומולי בגין דחיכון טעון אחרן ולא חלין חלקיא דיעקב כי חס כיוצר הכל הוא . רקיע אית לעילא על כל חלין רקיעין וחיא טמיר וגניזו ותמה דגנוטפכא דמשכח שלטא על האי רקיע והאי רקיע אקרי חילדא דמשכח ובהאי רקיע כל חינון חלונין מסטר' דא ומסטר' דא וחמיר כל חינון סדורין דמשכח שית חלונין אינון רברבין על כלהו וחד קאים לשלטא עלייהו . חלונא חדא אקרי חלון וכיף כפלא ככבא חדא לחקרי לאחזיי' לי' ודא חיה פתוח לקח מהתך לתתא כשלטנותא דיהוד' להו לחית ליה חולקא ביה דהא לית לשבטין דישראל חולקא ואחסנתא בהו חלא שבטא דיהודה שלטא על האי וחלו חיקו עלוהי וכל חסדו ככל יהוד' לרחיקו מכתר קדש בריך הוא חלו למדע <term>כתר</term> חלונא דא וקאי ככבא וחמרו דהא דא דקא מכנש לשאר עמין דכתיב ביה ילך כעיר חניניך וחולו חכתרי' ונבזן ליה סמושא ופולחנא ועל כתיב

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Tabernacle's construction from the previous section, specifically focusing on the mystical significance of the fifty hooks and their correspondence to the celestial firmaments and the tribes of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In the same blue manner as below, a vision is woven. For this manner was hinted at in the Book of King Solomon, regarding the wisdom of the precious sages, which was hidden from them—like the manner of the brilliance and flaming of known stars. These stars were not established by them, nor can they ever be fixed by them; rather, they were all established before Him for the restoration of the world, all of them to shine upon the earth as much as is needed to restore this world. It is written:

**And you shall make** fifty copper hooks, and it is written, *And you shall make fifty gold hooks* <note>Exodus 26:11 and 26:5</note>. We have learned: whoever has not seen those hooks has never seen the light of the stars in the firmament, because that vision and that manner resemble them to anyone who gazes upon them. Living stars in their firmament emerge from that firmament where all the stars shine. In that firmament, there are fifty <note>original: "חמש" (five), but contextually "חמשים" (fifty) based on the hooks</note> windows that are recessed, some on the eastern side and some on the southern side. In each and every window, there is one star. All the nations see through those windows and recesses in the firmament, which are like stars. And those stars emerge to be revealed from that gathering which was gathered and mixed in a blue manner; some are green like the color of gold, and therefore some are red and some are green. There are fifty in those windows on the other sides: on the eastern side they are green, and on the southern side they are red, like the initial redness that is found. All those stars that emerge from that firmament mingle at night, and they flame and rule in this world. Some rule over the blue and some over the green gold, and they are established and lead according to their power. These stars rule here and there <note>original: "פלוני" (so-and-so/specific place)</note> like the loops of the curtains for those moments of the hour. And those that lead the blue, they are like hooks and flame; and if their vision is seen three times on the eastern side, or five, or seven—kings of the nations will come against that side, and all wealth and gold will be removed from that side. But if they gather two, four, or six, one after the other, then wrath and visitation will fall and dwell upon that side with a good gathering and clarity. Wars will be stirred up but will not be carried out, for at that time there is an awakening above before the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>original: קב"ה</note> regarding those ministers who rule over the other nations; and so it is in this manner on the other side.

He opened and said:
> Let the name of God be blessed from eternity to eternity, for wisdom and might are His. <note>Daniel 2:20</note>

And He changes the times and the seasons, and all visions are like His garment. He uncovers the deep shell <note>original: קליפא (Kliphah) - the "husk" or "shell" of impurity in Kabbalah</note> from the sand and the crushing of the stars, and fills them, because those others are a burden; but not so is the Portion of Jacob, for He is the Creator of all. There is a firmament above all these firmaments, a hidden and concealed life. And wonder of wonders <note>original: גנוטפכא (a cryptic Zoharic term for a hidden treasure or vessel)</note> is found ruling over this firmament, and this firmament is called the "Skin of the Tabernacle." In this firmament are all those windows from this side and that side, and all those arrangements are strictly ordered. There are six windows that are greater than all of them, and one stands to rule over them. One window is called the "Window of the Double Cave" <note>original: וכיף כפלא (resembling Machpelah)</note>; one star is engraved to be seen there, and this is a living opening to receive from the flow below, like the sovereignty of Judah. The other nations have no portion in it, for the tribes of Israel have no portion or inheritance in them <note>the other stars</note>, except for the tribe of Judah who rules over this. And they are like hooks upon it, and all the kindness of Judah is to distance it from the Holy Crown <note>original: כתר (Keter)</note>. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, began to make known the <term>Crown</term> <note>The highest of the ten Sefirot, representing Divine Will</note> of this window. And the star stands in its fullness, for this is what gathers the rest of the nations, as it is written of him: *he shall go like a city of your grace* <note>alluding to the strength of Judah</note>. They give to him service and worship, and concerning this it is written:
> Then Judah approached him. <note>Genesis 44:18</note>

He drew near between them, for when this star emerges, it spreads one hand with five fingers, shining and gathering into that window.

<summary>This page explains the mystical correspondence between the fifty gold and copper hooks of the Tabernacle and the stars and "windows" of the celestial firmaments. It details how these heavenly bodies influence earthly kingdoms and highlights the unique spiritual status of the tribe of Judah.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**תרומה**<-

מאריכון דקוסמין ומרטין דאלי מאחי אתר בגין דבשעתא דהאי שלטא כלהו קמון
ומרטין תנכלהו ולא אזלא בידייהו ואי תימא ההוא רוחא דחזאי קאי רקיע טמירא היך
ידעי ליה. אלא מיכלא אית לון לבר וידעי דהאי שלטא בכלהו דא ולדא תדיר מיכא
ולא אזלא בידייהו אינון קסמין וחרטין. ועד אית זמנין דאזלון ביה בני נשא ואית
זמנין דלא אזלון ביה. ובגין דא אינון מארי קוסמין ומרטין מתמעטין מעבדייהו בגין
דלא ידעין עקרא כד מחאן דלא אזלא בידייהו. ועל דא אינון קדמאי הוו ידעי
ומסתכלן לבר בההוא מיכלא דקא ידעי. **חלונא תניינא** חקרי חלון טופרא בגין
דאיהו כגוונא דטופר' וביה נפקא ככבא חד דחקרי לחכימין נפצין דהא דא שלטא
בסולטאנו תקיף כדיכא. בריזא וכחשא אית ליה כנפצין כמין לקטא. מההוא חלון
נפקי שית מאה אלף רוחי רוזין דסלטין על אינון טופרי דבני נשא כד הזדרקן
כדתגלייא בהאי עבדי חרטין וקסמין כל אינון דידעי לון. בההוא שעתא דהאי
ככבא שלטא כל אינון דזרקי טופרייהו עביד חרטין גרים מיתא לכל עלמא וסליק
חרטין בידייהו דאינון דעבדי לון. **חלונא תליתאה** חקרי חלון מזבח וביה נפקא
ככבא חדא דחקרי בנב"ח <note>אולי צ"ל בינ"א</note> דכסיכא האי איהו כגונא דבנין וקיימ' על כל רוחא וכיוונא
וזכוותא ביה. לית ביה קטרוגא כלל כד איהו שלטא כל נייחא וכל נהירו שלטא
בעלמא סגיא טבאה וכלהו סליט בעלמא. **חלונא רביעאה** איהו חלון דחקרי נביט
וביה נפקא ככבא חד דחקרי לחכימין לאסכל בהפך בגין דסכיפיק כחלסול בנין
בזיזין כעכבין ככפרח בהאי אתערו דרחימ' תער בעלמא מרחיק ומקריב תולדות
פלוחי חסירותא בעלמא. בני עלמא לא קפדי כד אצטריכו ולא שלטו ומדנה אתער
בעלמ'. **חלונא חמישאה** איהו חלון דחקרי בחר על די ככבא דנפיק ביה עלה וכפיף
ליה כדי לא שליט לעלמין בהאי חכימי לבא לא יכלין למיק' בהרת קשוט בגין דלא
קאים בקיומיה ולא שכיך לעלמי'. ועד אשתדקן ברמייהו לעיינא בהאי אתר ולמילף
ליכא. **חלונא שתיתאה** איהו חלון דחקרי כנחא ונפקא ביה ככבא חד דחקרי
גירון בגין דכל האי שלטא עלמא קשיא כדיכא בכמה גזרין בכמה עונשין ובכל זינא
וזינא מתמדשן גזרין על עלמא ועד לא יסיימון אלין הא אחרנין מתחדשן וקאי דא
שלטא לא בעלמא. הכל סמוך ליומי משיחא ושלטא האי ארוכא כהאי ככבא על עלמ'.
ועל דא וסלטין מרטין ביזין על עלמא ויתחדשון זינין בישין דלא בתר דא ויטרש יהון
בעקני. וכל יתדקקון גו אטוכא כדין יכסר לון קב"ה <note>קדוש ברוך הוא</note> נהירו דוימחו ויקבלון מלכותא
קדישי עליונין וכדין **חלונא שביעאה** ותפתח בכל עלמא וככבא דיליה יהא נהיר
לרבעין זווין. וכד יתגלי מלכא משיחא ויתכנשון לגבי מלכא משיחא כל עמין דעלמ'
כדין יתקיים קרא דכתיב:

> **שרש ישי אשר עמד לנס עמים אליו גוים ידרשו והיתה מנוחתו כבוד.** <note>ישעיהו יא, י</note>

פתח ואמר ולא אמר ליה אלא לזל עיני כונן זמירות כולה'. האי קרא
אוקמוה ואתמר. הכל עזטי עזטי תבעי ליה חלן עזטי אלא סמא דאלוד סמא כלא
איהו ליתקנא אולא ובי דיניה. דא סמא סלים איהו דכליל דכר ונוקבא ח"ל ול' ובניני
כך עזטי. כיננא זמירות כולהא בגין דהא הוא דקא משבחת תדיר לנבי מלכא דעלמא
ליויה כגוונא דכנופיא דלא שכיך תדיר בגין לקבלא נהורא קדוש על כל מתנילות

<meta>This page continues the discussion of celestial mysteries within the portion of Terumah, specifically detailing the seven "windows" (Chalonot) in the heavens and the stars that emerge from them to govern earthly affairs. It follows the previous descriptions of spiritual hierarchies and transitions into the signs preceding the Messianic era.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah**<-

The masters of sorcery and divination <note>original: "qosemin ve-chartin"</note> are seized by this place, for at the time when this [celestial power] rules, they all stand in confusion and their divinations do not succeed in their hands. And if you say: that hidden spirit which is seen in the firmament, how do they know it? Rather, they have a sign outside, and they know that this one rules over all of them, and this is born constantly from here, and those sorceries and divinations do not succeed in their hands. And yet there are times when people follow it, and times when they do not. Because of this, those masters of sorcery and divination are diminished in their works, because they do not know the root when they are struck so that [the power] does not succeed in their hands. Regarding this, the ancients knew and looked outward at that sign which they knew.

**The second window** is called the "Nail Window" <note>original: "Chalon Tofra"</note> because it is shaped like a fingernail. Through it emerges a single star which the wise call "The Scatterer," for it rules with a powerful dominion like a hammer. In its secret and its movement, it has sparks like a collection of smithereens. From that window emerge six hundred thousand hidden spirits that rule over the fingernails of people when they are thrown away, as is revealed in this; through these, the sorcerers and diviners perform their works, all those who know them. At the time when this star rules, all those who throw away their nail parings cause sorcery to bring death to the entire world, and the sorcery succeeds in the hands of those who perform it.

**The third window** is called the "Altar Window." Through it emerges a single star called Binah <note>The text reads "NB"Ch," but a note suggests it should be "Binah," meaning Understanding</note> which is hidden. This is like a building, and it stands over every spirit and direction, and merit is found within it. There is no accusation <note>prosecuting angel</note> in it at all. When it rules, all rest and all light rule in the world, great goodness, and all [blessings] rule in the world.

**The fourth window** is the window called "The Gaze" <note>original: "Navit"</note>. Through it emerges a single star which the wise call "The Inverse," because it is bent like a hook, with broken structures like spiders or like blossoms. Through this, love is awakened in the world, distancing and bringing near the offspring of those who serve [the idols of] deficiency in the world. The people of the world are not careful when they are needed and do not rule, and from this, [strife] is awakened in the world.

**The fifth window** is the window called "In the Sea" <note>original: "Be-Char"</note>. Regarding the star that emerges through it, it rises and bends so that it never rules. In this, the wise of heart cannot stand upon the true appearance, because it does not remain in its standing and is never still. And they still labor in their deceptions to gaze into this place, but there is nothing to learn.

**The sixth window** is the window called "The Gathering" <note>original: "Kanacha"</note>. Through it emerges a single star called "The Throat" <note>original: "Giron"</note>, because all its rule over the world is harsh, with many decrees and many punishments. Each and every kind of decree is renewed upon the world, and before these are finished, others are renewed. This rule does not [usually] stand in the world. All this is close to the days of the Messiah, and this long [star] rules like this star over the world. And because of this, the masters of divination will be despised in the world, and evil types [of decrees] will be renewed one after another, and they will be troubled in their hardships. All will be crushed within the darkness. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, will prepare for them a light that will wipe them out, and the high holy ones will receive the kingdom. And then **the seventh window** will open to all the world, and its star will shine to the four corners. And when the King Messiah is revealed, all the nations of the world will gather to the King Messiah, then the scripture will be fulfilled as it is written:

> **"And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious."** <note>Isaiah 11:10</note>

He opened and said: He did not say it except to the one whose eyes are fixed on the melodies of all. This verse has been established and explained. Everything requires great strength <note>original: "azti"</note>, but the medicine of the birth, the medicine of everything, is to prepare the beginning and its house of judgment. This is a complete medicine that includes male and female... He established all the melodies because she is the one who constantly praises the King of the world, like a gathering that is never still, in order to receive the holy light upon all the teachings.

->**163**<-

## Main Text (Zohar)

חדוה. וכל אינון זמירות כל אינון ככביא דקא מנהרן ברקיעא כלהו אזלן ומשבחן לקב"ה <note>לקודשא בריך הוא</note> ככל ההוא זמנא דאתחזון ברקיעא. בגין דמלאכי עלאי כלהו אזלן ומשבחן ואמרין תשבחות בתלת פלגי דהוי לילייא. בלילייא אתפלגן כמה סטרין ברשותיה דליליא כד רמז לליליא והא אתמשך כל אינון רוחין בישין ודינין בישין כלהו מתבדרן ומשטטן בכל עלמא ואתפרשן סטרא אחרא ותכשי חרמיה דבי מלכא מכל אינון סטרין קדישין. כיון דההוא סטרא אחרא אתער כל בני עלמא טעמי טעמא דמותא חד מסתין במוהא וסלקין עלייהו. כדין כיון דמשכחו לתפרשא לעילא ושלטו ונחתו לתתא כדין אתפרשן תלת סטרין לאכחא ליה לקב"ה כתלת סטרין דליליא כמה דאתערן כלהו. בעוד דאינון משכחן לקב"ה סטרא אחרא אזלא ומשטטא לתתא בכל סטרי עלמא. ועד דסטרא אחרא לא אתעבר מתמן לא יכלין אינון להתייחדא במאריהון רוח לחכימין. מלאכי עילאיין וישראל לתתא כלהו דחקי בההוא סטרא אחרא. מלאכין עלאין כד בעיין לאתאחדא במאריהון לא יכלין עד דדחיין לה לבר מה עבדין אותין זיקין דנור דמלאכי קדישי וסחיפו טיבותא על כל בני עלמא וכד חיקו כעתא דקא דחיין לה לבר ויהבי לה כל עלמא דא בההוא טיבתא כדין חיקו סלקא עלייהו ומקבלין מסחבו מוסף. בר בלחוד דישראל בלחודיהו דלא סלטין תמן בגין דאיהי אתפרשא מכייהו עיין לקמי מאריהון ומשבחן וסלדן קמיה. כגוונא דא ישראל לתתא לא יכלין להתייחדא במאריהון עד דדחיין לההוא סטרא אחרא מכייהו ויהבי לה חולקא כמה דאתערת פלגת לאינון מתקרבין לגבי מאריהון ולא אשתכח מקטרגא עילא ותתא. ואי תימא תינח לתתא אבל לעילא מאי קטרוגא תמן. אלא לעילא בגין דאיהו רוח מסאבא ואינון רוחין קדישין עד דמטרדי רוחא מסאבא מכייהו לא יכלין לקרבא לגבי מאריהון דהא קב"ה גו מסאבא לא מתערב לעלמין. וכן כגוונא דא ישראל לתתא. ותרין סטרין עלאין ותתאין כד בעיין לקרבא לגבי מלכא קדישא דחיין לה לבר. ועל כל עיול לילייא ומלאכין קדישין עלאין כד מסתדרן שורין שורין לקרבא לגבי מאריהון דחיין ליה לההוא סטרא לבר כדקדמיתא ולכת עשין לקב"ה. ועל דא כד עיול לילייא כל רוחין בישין וזיקין ודינין מסחבי ומתחזיין לבר וסחטי מלכו עילון גו קדשא. למלכא דהוו ליה חכמין יקירין כמה תיבותא מתגלפי בקומסטלויי. וההוא מלכא הוה חכים בגין דלא יתקרב כל מחז דבי מלכא סתים תיבותא דחכמין יקירין ומרנזן דתמן כטל בחכמתיה חד חיויא תקיפא וכריך ליה סוחרניה דההוא תיבותא. כל מאן דבעי להוסטא ידיה לגבי תיבותא הא חיויא דנא עליה וקטיל ליה. חד רחימא הוה ליה למלכא אמר ליה מלכא כל זמנא דאת בעי למעיל ולאשתמשא בתיבותא תעביד כך וכך לגבי ההוא חיויא ותפתח תיבותא ותשמש בגניזין דילי. כך קב"ה כריך מיזא דמרכבה דקדשא לתתא מלאכין עלאין לעילא גו קדשא הא חיויא תמן ודקלא לאסתכלא ביה. ואי תימא הא כלהו חטא וחטא לא מקבלי חסרנו. תא חזי כתיב 
> עשה מלאכיו רוחות משרתיו אש להט <note>תהלים קד:ד</note>
עשה מלאכיו רוחות אלין מלאכין דקיימין לבר. משרתיו אש להט אלין מלאכין דקיימין גו חיויא רוחין מסחבי ואינון רוחי. רוח ברוח לא עייל דא בדא. רוח מסחבא ברוח קדשא לא אתערבו.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the spiritual mechanics of the night, specifically focusing on the transition from the songs of the stars to the emergence of the "Other Side" (Sitra Achra) and how both angels and Israel must navigate this impurity to reach the Divine.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Joy. And all those songs of all those stars that shine in the firmament, all of them go and praise the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> throughout the entire time they are visible in the firmament. Because the high angels all go and praise and say songs of praise during the three watches of the night. At night, many sides are divided under the authority of the Night; when He signals to the Night, all those evil spirits and evil judgments are drawn out, spreading and roaming throughout the entire world. The "Other Side" <note>The *Sitra Achra*, representing the forces of impurity or evil</note> separates itself and prepares its nets <note>or "traps"</note> away from the King’s palace and from all those holy sides. Once that Other Side is awakened, all the inhabitants of the world taste the taste of death <note>A reference to sleep being one-sixtieth of death</note>, as it hovers over them and ascends upon them. Then, since they find themselves separated above, and they rule and descend below, they then divide into three sides to oppose the Holy One, blessed be He, corresponding to the three watches of the night as they are all awakened. While they find the Holy One, blessed be He, the Other Side goes and roams below in all the regions of the world. And until the Other Side is removed from there, they cannot unite with their Master—a spirit for the wise. The high angels and Israel below all press against that Other Side. When the high angels desire to unite with their Master, they cannot until they push her <note>the Other Side</note> outside. What do they do? They produce sparks of fire—those holy angels—and they sweep goodness over all the inhabitants of the world. And when they push her outside and give her this world with that "goodness" <note>referring to the physical husks or distractions</note>, then they ascend and receive additional holiness. Except for Israel alone, over whom she does not rule, because she is separated from them; they look toward their Master, praising and trembling before Him. In this same manner, Israel below cannot unite with their Master until they push that Other Side away from them and give her a portion <note>A reference to certain rituals, like the scapegoat or the washing of fingers, intended to "bribe" the accuser</note> as has been explained, so that those who draw near to their Master are divided and no accuser is found above or below. And if you say, "That is fine for below, but above, what accusation could there be?" Rather, above, because it is an impure spirit, and those are holy spirits—until they remove the impure spirit from among them, they cannot draw near to their Master, for the Holy One, blessed be He, never mixes with impurity. And so it is for Israel below. Both sides, above and below, when they seek to draw near to the Holy King, push her outside. At the onset of the night, when the holy high angels arrange themselves in rows upon rows to draw near to their Master, they push that Side outside as before and perform the will of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore, when night begins, all the evil spirits, sparks, and judgments are made impure and appear outside, and they squeeze the heavenly kingdom within the holiness. This is like a King who had precious wise men and many treasures engraved in chests. And that King was wise; so that no one would approach the King's hidden treasures—the chests of the precious wise men where the "dew of wisdom" is stored—he placed a powerful serpent <note>original: *chivya*</note> in his wisdom, and it coiled around that chest. Anyone who sought to stretch out his hand toward the chest, this serpent would fall upon him and kill him. The King had one friend; the King said to him, "Whenever you wish to enter and use the chest, do such-and-through to that serpent, and you shall open the chest and use my hidden treasures." So the Holy One, blessed be He, coiled the "husk" of the Holy Chariot <note>The *Merkavah* or Divine Assembly</note> below, and the high angels above within the holiness—behold, the serpent is there, and it is difficult to look upon it. And if you say, "Behold, they all sin and do not receive their lack," come and see what is written:
> "He makes the winds His messengers, flaming fire His ministers" <note>Psalms 104:4</note>
"He makes the winds His messengers"—these are the angels who stand outside. "Flaming fire His ministers"—these are the angels who stand within the serpent, the impure spirits, and they are spirits. Spirit does not enter into spirit; an impure spirit and a holy spirit do not mix.

<summary>This page explains that the "Other Side" (Sitra Achra) acts as a protective, albeit dangerous, barrier around divine holiness, much like a serpent guarding a king's treasure. It describes how angels and Israel must "bribe" or push away this impurity to achieve spiritual union with the Creator during the night watches.</summary>
